info.name: Argentum API — /v1
info.description:
Generated from apps/backend/openapi/v1.yaml (contract version 2026-07-30).

Do not edit by hand — run `pnpm --filter @argentum/openapi-tools build` and commit the result.

Set `apiKey` in the environment first. `GET /v1/me` is the call to make before any other:
it tells you which scopes your key has, what it may spend, and which contract version you
are talking to.

item.name: Identity
item.description: Who this key is, and what it may spend.

item.name: The key, its scopes, its rate limit, and the tenant's credit position

request.description:
The first call to make and the one paste that makes a support question
answerable. It needs no scope — a key with none must still be able to
find out that it has none.

Scope: none — any key reaches this route.

item.name: Spend over a window, and what is left

query.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Defaults to the first of the current UTC month.
End of the window, exclusive. Defaults to the first of next UTC month. Must be after `from`, and no more than 366 days later.

request.description:
What this workspace has spent between `from` and `to`, and the credit
position at the moment of the call.

This is not `GET /v1/me` with more fields. `/v1/me` answers "can I make
a call at all", in one paste, with no period attached to the number.
This answers "what did my integration cost over the period I bill my own
users for" — a window the caller chooses, broken down by model, which is
what an application reselling these answers needs in order to meter its
own users.

Both bounds default to the current calendar month in UTC, which is the
period a monthly grant is measured against. `from` is inclusive and `to`
is exclusive.

Scope: `read:usage`

item.name: Reports
item.description: A spec in and a file out, or a prompt in and a turn behind it.

item.name: Ask an agent for a report

header.description: A unique string per logical request; a UUID is the usual choice. Both

request.description:
A prompt in, a real agent turn behind it, a document at the end. Seconds
to minutes, priced in tokens.

Three ways to collect the result, and a caller picks one: poll
`GET /v1/reports/{id}`, stream `GET /v1/reports/{id}/events`, or supply
a `callback_url` and verify the signature described by
`GET /v1/me`'s `webhooks` block.

Scope: `write:reports`

Once `status` is `completed` the `document` block carries a freshly
presigned `download_url`. It is re-issued on every read rather than
stored, so a caller who saved one and came back an hour later gets a
working link without paying to regenerate the document.

Scope: `read:documents`

Server-sent events for a job that can take minutes. Two event names:
`progress` while the agent works, and `report` — terminal — carrying the
same object `GET /v1/reports/{id}` returns.

The agent's token deltas are deliberately not forwarded: a report's
consumer wants progress and a file, not the prose of an answer they
asked for as a PDF.

A job that had already finished when the caller connected gets its
`report` frame and nothing else. A queued *render* job has no thread to
publish on, so it gets the same — poll that one.

Scope: `read:documents`

item.name: Render a document from a spec

header.description: A unique string per logical request; a UUID is the usual choice. Both

request.description:
Deterministic. A spec goes in, a file comes out, and nothing about it
touches an LLM or a thread.

**`Accept` decides the response body.** `application/json` (or an absent
`Accept`) returns the document object with a short-lived presigned URL.
The format's own content type — `application/pdf`, `text/csv`, the two
OOXML types — or `application/octet-stream` returns the bytes inline,
which is what a caller writing them straight to disk wants.

A spec that outruns the synchronous window becomes a job and answers
`202` with a report object, on the same shape `POST /v1/reports`
returns. Write one collection path for both.

Scope: `write:reports`

request.description:
Newest first, cursor-paginated.

**No download URLs on the list.** Presigning is a signature per row, and
a caller paging a hundred documents to find one is not about to fetch
all hundred. `GET /v1/documents/{id}` issues the URL for the one they
picked.

Scope: `read:documents`

item.name: Fetch one document's metadata and a fresh download URL

request.description:
Streams the object rather than redirecting to the presigned URL. A
server-side HTTP client that does not follow redirects — a deliberate
setting in plenty of them — would otherwise write three hundred bytes of
nothing to disk, and the redirect is a second hostname the caller's
egress rules have to allow.

Scope: `read:documents`

item.name: Chat
item.description: A question in, an answer out.

header.description: A unique string per logical request; a UUID is the usual choice. Both
The `id:` of the last frame you received. An SSE client sends this by

request.description:
**`Accept` decides the door.** `text/event-stream` streams the turn as
it is written; anything else blocks until the turn answers.

A client disconnect never cancels a turn: the agent runs in the worker
and this route is a reader of the same bus the dashboard reads. Hanging
up ends the read, the turn finishes, the answer persists, and
`GET /v1/threads/{id}/messages` collects it.

The synchronous door answers **504** when the turn outruns the wait —
not when the turn fails. That response carries `in_flight.thread_id`,
and it **keeps its idempotency key**, so the retry a 504 invites replays
instead of starting a second billed turn. Attach to
`GET /v1/threads/{id}/events` instead.

Scope: `write:chat`

Only threads belonging to this end user.

request.description:
`api` threads only. A machine credential that could list the dashboard's
threads would let a leaked key read the staff's own chat history.

Scope: `read:threads`

query.description: When present, the thread must belong to this end user or the route

request.description:
`write:chat` rather than `read:threads`: destroying a conversation is
not a read. Saved dashboards the turns produced are removed with it.

Scope: `write:chat`

query.description: When present, the thread must belong to this end user or the route

item.name: Attach to a thread's newest turn

header.description: The `id:` of the last frame you received. An SSE client sends this by

query.description: When present, the thread must belong to this end user or the route

request.description:
The resume door. A 504 from the synchronous send and a
`409 request_in_flight` from a retried one both hand back a `thread_id`,
and neither is collectable by re-POSTing — one turn is already running,
and starting a second is what the whole idempotency chain exists to
prevent. This is where a caller goes instead.

If the thread's newest turn has already answered, the answer is
delivered and the stream closes. Send `Last-Event-ID` to have the
messages you missed replayed first.

Scope: `read:threads`

request.description:
Public and keyless: an integrator reads the contract before they have a
credential to call it with. It is the same bytes as
`apps/backend/openapi/v1.yaml`, converted to JSON.

It is still behind the `/v1` kill switch. A spec for a surface that is
refusing every call would generate a client nobody can use, so a
disabled deployment answers 503 here too.

Scope: none — any key reaches this route.
